# Prepare and submit a public procurement bid

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When the company is considering a government or other formal tender opportunity. An authorized compliant submission or documented no-bid decision with obligations and evaluation follow-up assigned.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> Operational draft. Source checked on 2026-10-30. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance, certification or completed execution is claimed. The source context is UK tender example; buyer-specific rules govern. Resolve applicable law and expert review before external action.

- An authorized compliant submission or documented no-bid decision with obligations and evaluation follow-up assigned.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Extract the tender requirements and timetable

agent-runnable


Read the buyer-issued documents and amendments. Record eligibility, submission channel, evaluation criteria, required evidence and the stated deadline with its timezone.

- Sources: [UK SME and VCSE public procurement bid pack](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/smevcse-public-procurement-bid-pack/smevcse-bid-pack)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Approve a bid or no-bid decision

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The accountable owner reviews qualification, delivery capacity, commercial risk and conflicts. Obtain specialist interpretation for unfamiliar procurement rules and decline opportunities whose mandatory requirements cannot be met.

- Sources: [UK SME and VCSE public procurement bid pack](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/smevcse-public-procurement-bid-pack/smevcse-bid-pack)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Assemble the evidence and response matrix

agent-runnable


Map each question and criterion to a specific response, supporting evidence and responsible reviewer. Mark missing certifications or references explicitly rather than making unsupported compliance claims.

- Sources: [UK SME and VCSE public procurement bid pack](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/smevcse-public-procurement-bid-pack/smevcse-bid-pack)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Review pricing commitments and declarations

human · human approval required · hard to undo


Authorized commercial and technical reviewers approve delivery promises, pricing assumptions and contractual departures. Check representations and required signatures against the actual company facts.

- Sources: [UK SME and VCSE public procurement bid pack](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/smevcse-public-procurement-bid-pack/smevcse-bid-pack)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Submit the approved bid through the buyer channel

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


An authorized submitter uploads the approved version and retains the receipt and timestamp. Keep access credentials private and verify accepted submission status before the deadline.

- Sources: [UK SME and VCSE public procurement bid pack](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/smevcse-public-procurement-bid-pack/smevcse-bid-pack)

<a id="step-6"></a>

### 6. Manage clarification and award decisions

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The bid owner controls responses and records evaluation outcomes. A successful bid does not authorize signing an unreviewed contract; route awards and material amendments through their required approvals.

- Verify: An authorized compliant submission or documented no-bid decision with obligations and evaluation follow-up assigned.
- Sources: [UK SME and VCSE public procurement bid pack](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/smevcse-public-procurement-bid-pack/smevcse-bid-pack)
